bullets.title: NVDA: BofA Sum-of-Parts Sees 34–50% Upside; Bearish Flow Dominates Today
bullets.body: Bank of America's sum-of-parts analysis on Nvidia's free cash flow suggests the stock trades at a 34–50% discount to fair value, with AI risks viewed as overblown. Separately, NVDA registered the most bearish options flow of any stock today, and a tweet flagged Jensen Huang's reduction of the Ohio data center commitment from $250B to $105B while pressuring private credit firms to fund a $500B SPV replacement—raising questions about undisclosed strategic drivers.

bullets.title: NVDA: Ben Thompson Says Price Cuts Happening Via Financing, Not List Price
bullets.body: Citing Ben Thompson's Stratechery analysis, multiple accounts flagged that Nvidia is effectively cutting prices through circular customer-financing structures rather than reducing official list prices, implying margin compression that won't show up in headline ASP data. The move reflects intensifying competitive dynamics.

bullets.title: FN Earnings Beat: +45% Revenue Growth, Data Center at 51% of Mix
bullets.body: Fabrinet reported Q4 revenue of $1.316B, +45% YoY, above guidance, with adj. EPS of $4.10. Data Center revenue surged 68% YoY to $669M (51% of total), with new 800G hyperscaler-direct ramps beginning. Q1 guide of $1.375–$1.425B implies ~43% YoY growth at the midpoint.

bullets.title: META Down 16%+ YTD, Worst Year Since 2022; Youth Exploitation Trial Underway
bullets.body: META has spent most of 2026 below its 200-day moving average and is down over 16% YTD—its worst performance since the 74% drawdown in 2022. A major multistate trial kicked off Tuesday with prosecutors alleging the company deliberately 'hooked and exploited' children and misled the public; META shares fell 3.8% on the session to a two-week low.

bullets.title: TSLA Bulls vs. Reality: FCF Swings to -$9.7B, Autonomy Thesis Questioned
bullets.body: Multiple accounts pushed back hard on Tesla bull thesis: per Bloomberg data, TSLA FCF is projected to swing from +$3.6B in 2021 to -$9.7B in 2026. The stock has also underperformed the Nasdaq-100 by nearly 2x over five years (+51% vs. +98%). Skeptics argue competitors will solve autonomy alongside Tesla, making the Cybercab narrative unsupported by evidence.

bullets.title: TSLA Semi: Einride Orders 500 Trucks in Largest Public Commitment
bullets.body: Einride agreed to purchase 500 Tesla Semi trucks for U.S. operations, the largest public commitment to the electric truck. First deliveries begin next month, with remaining units arriving in phases over 24 months.

bullets.title: AAPL: EU App Store Overhaul Takes Effect October 1—New Fee Tiers Detailed
bullets.body: Apple announced a comprehensive restructuring of EU App Store terms effective October 1: in-app purchases carry a 26% commission, alternative payment methods face a 20% fee, apps linking to external purchase pages pay 15%, and the Core Technology Fee is replaced by a 5% commission on out-of-app digital transactions. Apple also broadened access to alternative app marketplaces and added under-18 safety protections.

bullets.title: AAPL: Congress Pressures Apple to Pledge No Chinese Memory Chips
bullets.body: U.S. Congress is reportedly requesting Apple sign a written pledge not to use Chinese memory chips, even as SK Hynix invests in U.S. fabs. The move reflects escalating geopolitical pressure on Apple's supply chain sourcing decisions.

bullets.title: SNDK Up 62% from July Lows on 6-Day Win Streak; Technicals Bullish
bullets.body: SanDisk is up 62% since its July low and on a 6-day winning streak, trading above its 20-, 100-, and 200-day moving averages. One trader implied further upside toward all-time highs given the technical setup.

bullets.title: AI Semis vs. SaaS: Observers Note Inverse Correlation Suggesting Institutional Unwind
bullets.body: A trader flagged a pattern over recent months where GAI infrastructure names (NVDA, MU, SNDK, LITE) sell off while SaaS rallies—suggesting coordinated unwinding of long-GAI/short-SaaS institutional positions rather than fundamental news flow.

bullets.title: LLM Model-Layer Revenue: $423B Run-Rate Central Case by December 2027
bullets.body: One account published a global LLM model-layer revenue projection: central case of $422.8B annualized run-rate by December 2027, with a bear case of $254.3B and bull case of $703.5B. The analysis is framed as bullish for NVDA, MU, SNDK, and LITE.

bullets.title: AAOI: Sold Out of Capacity, US Production Premiums Positive for ASPs/Margins
bullets.body: AAOI Rosenblatt Summit notes: company is sold out of current capacity, expects premiums for U.S. production of 800G/1.6T. Multiple LTAs under discussion but management is avoiding signing deals that could block capacity for higher-value customers including NVDA-adjacent opportunities.

bullets.title: Optical NPO/CPO Attach Rates to Rise Slowly Due to Manufacturing Constraints
bullets.body: A supply-chain research note flagged that manufacturing—not demand—remains the binding constraint for NPO/CPO products. Higher attach rates will grow more slowly than market expectations, with multiple supply-chain visits confirming capacity constraints.

bullets.title: GOOGL Plans to Exit China for Pixel Manufacturing by 2027
bullets.body: Google is reportedly shifting its entire Pixel smartphone, watch, and earbud production out of China by 2027, targeting Vietnam and India as primary new manufacturing destinations—consistent with broader tech supply-chain diversification.

bullets.title: AMZN Expands Louisiana Data Center Investment from $12B to $18B
bullets.body: Amazon announced it is increasing its planned Louisiana data center investment from $12B to $18B, adding a third campus. The move underscores continued hyperscaler infrastructure buildout momentum.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Debt Issuance Approaching Major-Bank Scale in IG Bond Market
bullets.body: One macro observer noted that hyperscalers are issuing investment-grade debt at a scale approaching that of major banks, a trend that could materialize fully within a few years. Separately, Charlie Bilello's work on off-balance-sheet AI commitments suggests nine major tech companies have ~$3 trillion in AI-related spending not captured in reported capex.

bullets.title: 30-Year Treasury Hits Multi-Decade High; Goldman Warns Fed May Be Forced to Hike
bullets.body: The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.31%, its highest since June 2007, while the 10-year hit 4.75%—a 19-month high. Goldman Sachs' Delta-One desk warned the Fed may be forced to hike amid global bond market stress. Ed Yardeni identified 5% on the 10-year as the key threshold that would signal a problem; the current level of 4.75% is not yet alarming in his view.

bullets.title: Geopolitical Risk: UAE Intercepts Iranian Missiles; Diesel Margins Hit Record $102/bbl
bullets.body: UAE defense ministry confirmed detection of two Iranian ballistic missiles; a tanker attack was also reported in the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. diesel refining margins surged to a record $102/barrel, driven by Hormuz supply disruptions and Ukrainian strikes on Russian infrastructure. Trump stated no Iran talks are underway while claiming all Hormuz mines have been cleared.

bullets.title: US Housing Starts Plunge 12.4% in July; Pending Home Sales Miss Again
bullets.body: July housing starts fell 12.4% to 1.239M units, well below the 1.345M consensus and approaching COVID-era lows. July pending home sales dropped 2.3% MoM vs. flat expectations, hitting the lowest level since January. Building permits were the lone bright spot, beating at 1.443M vs. 1.375M expected.

bullets.title: SPY Gamma Flip: $2.3B Put Wall at 765; $20M Unusual Put Buying in SPY and MU
bullets.body: Options activity flags a $2.3B put wall at SPY 765 after a gamma flip, and a separate ~$20M unusual put purchase was detected across SPY and MU, suggesting traders are positioning for downside in both the broad market and memory semiconductors. SPY was also on track to close below its 8-day EMA for the first time in three weeks.
